lines: This is Better Ragdoll: a free Blender extension that makes ragdolls fall like real bodies, not like puppets.
Most ragdolls only use hard joint limits. Every joint swings at full speed, then stops dead at its limit, so the body flops around and bounces off its own joints.
Better Ragdoll adds soft limits. Near the end of its range, each joint meets growing resistance, like muscles and tendons stretching, so it slows down before it gets there.

It also adds a gentle pull toward a relaxed posture, inspired by NASA's neutral body posture. In zero gravity, the classic ragdoll just drifts in its T-pose, while Better Ragdoll curls into the pose a body takes when every muscle is relaxed.
Now push both down the stairs. The classic ragdoll flails like a puppet. Better Ragdoll tumbles with weight, and comes to rest in a believable pose.
Impacts also kick the shoulders and hips. Arms fly with the push, legs swing the other way, with a touch of randomness so no two falls look the same.
Setup takes one click. Detect the bones, pick a release frame and an impact, then simulate and bake to an action. Better Ragdoll: free and open source, for Blender 4.2 and up.
